text:
# Five Punnett Square Problems: Incomplete Dominance

---

**Problem 1: Snapdragon Flower Color**

In snapdragons, red flower color (RR) and white flower color (WW) are homozygous. Heterozygous plants (RW) produce pink flowers. Cross a pink snapdragon with a white snapdragon.

Parent 1: RW (pink)
Parent 2: WW (white)

|  | W | W |
|---|---|---|
| R | RW | RW |
| W | WW | WW |

Offspring: 2 RW (pink) and 2 WW (white)
Phenotype ratio: 1 pink : 1 white (50% pink and 50% white)

---

**Problem 2: Andalusian Chicken Feather Color**

In Andalusian chickens, black feathers (BB) crossed with white feathers (WW) produce blue feathered offspring (BW). Cross two blue chickens.

Parent 1: BW (blue)
Parent 2: BW (blue)

|  | B | W |
|---|---|---|
| B | BB | BW |
| W | BW | WW |

Offspring: 1 BB (black) and 2 BW (blue) and 1 WW (white)
Phenotype ratio: 1 black : 2 blue : 1 white (25% black and 50% blue and 25% white)

---

**Problem 3: Carnation Petal Color**

In carnations, red petals (CR CR) crossed with white petals (CW CW) produce pink petals (CR CW). Cross a red carnation with a pink carnation.

Parent 1: CR CR (red)
Parent 2: CR CW (pink)

|  | CR | CW |
|---|---|---|
| CR | CR CR | CR CW |
| CR | CR CR | CR CW |

Offspring: 2 CR CR (red) and 2 CR CW (pink)
Phenotype ratio: 1 red : 1 pink (50% red and 50% pink)

---

**Problem 4: Radish Shape**

In radishes, round shape (RR) crossed with long shape (LL) produces oval offspring (RL). A farmer crosses two oval radishes.

Parent 1: RL (oval)
Parent 2: RL (oval)

|  | R | L |
|---|---|---|
| R | RR | RL |
| L | RL | LL |

Offspring: 1 RR (round) and 2 RL (oval) and 1 LL (long)
Phenotype ratio: 1 round : 2 oval : 1 long (25% round and 50% oval and 25% long)

---

**Problem 5: Shorthorn Cattle Coat Color**

In Shorthorn cattle, red coat (RR) crossed with white coat (WW) produces roan coat (RW), which looks like a mix of red and white hairs. A rancher crosses a roan cow with a red bull.

Parent 1: RW (roan)
Parent 2: RR (red)

|  | R | R |
|---|---|---|
| R | RR | RR |
| W | RW | RW |

Offspring: 2 RR (red) and 2 RW (roan)
Phenotype ratio: 1 red : 1 roan (50% red and 50% roan)

---

## Quick Reference for Students

In incomplete dominance, the heterozygous phenotype is a blend of the two homozygous phenotypes. Neither allele is fully dominant. Three phenotypes are possible instead of two.

**How to tell it is incomplete dominance:** The heterozygote looks different from both homozygotes, usually appearing as a blend or intermediate form.
